statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the implementation allows any header to be retrieved, it MUST NOT include any header names in the list but MUST include the special entry ":" (a single colon on its own).
actions: Omit all individual header names from the LIST HEADERS response list

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the implementation allows any header to be retrieved, it MUST NOT include any header names in the list but MUST include the special entry ":" (a single colon on its own).
actions: Include the special entry ":" in the LIST HEADERS response list

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MUST still explicitly list any metadata items that are available.
actions: Explicitly enumerate all available metadata items in the LIST HEADERS response list

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The list MAY be empty (though in this circumstance there is little point in providing the HDR command).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An implementation that also supports the OVER command SHOULD at least permit all the headers and metadata items listed in the output from the LIST OVERVIEW.FMT command.
actions: Permit via HDR at minimum all headers and metadata items listed in LIST OVERVIEW.FMT output

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the MSGID argument is specified, the results MUST be those available for the first form of the HDR command.
actions: Return fields available for the message-id form of the HDR command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the RANGE argument is specified, the results MUST be those available for the second and third forms of the HDR command.
actions: Return fields available for the range and current-article-number forms of the HDR command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If no argument is specified, the results MUST be those available in all forms of the HDR command (that is, it MUST only list those items listed in both the previous cases).
actions: Return fields available across all forms of the HDR command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If no argument is specified, the results MUST be those available in all forms of the HDR command (that is, it MUST only list those items listed in both the previous cases).
actions: Include only those items present in both the MSGID-form result set and the RANGE-form result set

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server does not treat the various forms differently, then it MUST ignore any argument and always produce the same results (though not necessarily always in the same order).
actions: Ignore any argument supplied to LIST HEADERS
Produce the same result set regardless of argument value
